minutes_text:
CITY COUNCIL
MINUTES
CITY OF BALDWIN PARK
CITY COUNCIL
WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 07, 2009
7:00 p.m. COUNCIL CHAMBERS
14403 E. Pacific Avenue
Baldwin Park
Manuel Lozano, Mayor
Marlen Garcia, Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia, Ricardo Pacheco, Susan Rubio, Council Members
Maria Contreras, City Treasurer Alejandra Avila, City Clerk
The CITY COUNCIL of the City of Baldwin Park met in REGULAR SESSION at the above time and place.
CALL TO ORDER
INVOCATION
Led by Council member Bejarano
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
ROLL CALL
Present: None.
Absent: Council member Pacheco.
Also Present: City Treasurer Contreras, City Clerk Rubio, Deputy City Clerk Nieto, Community Development Manager Marc Castagnola, Council member Marlen Garcia, Director of Public Works William Galvez, Chief of Police Lili Hadsell, City Attorney Joseph W. Pannone, Director of Recreation & Community Services Manuel Carrillo Jr., Chief Executive Officer Vijay Singhal, Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia, Council member Bejarano, Mayor Lozano, Director of Finance Lorena Quijano.
Council member Pacheco arrived at 7:05 p.m.
ANNOUNCEMENTS
NONE
PROCLAMATIONS, COMMENDATIONS & PRESENTATIONS
NONE
PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS
Thomas Cary , resident spoke about various issues related to the enforcement of illegal workers; animal control; and pedestrian safety
Patricia Jimenez , resident requested that the city look into the flooding situation near the cul-de-sac by Foster Elementary
Al Contreras , resident announced the upcoming Water Fest and 5K Walk; he also announced a free toilet give-away event
Rafael Gonzalez , library manager announced an upcoming event and welcomed donations; he thanked Recreation & Community Services Director Carrillo for placing the event on the marquee at Morgan Park
Edward Martinez , resident thanked the Council for implementing the community cable channel
Patty Rascon , property owner addressed the discussion item on the agenda regarding Council member Pacheco . She expressed her opinion that the Council had acted rudely towards the public and that the audience should be treated with respect
Johnny Rios , resident thanked Chief Executive Officer Singhal and Director of Recreation & Community Services Carrillo for the improvements being done at Walnut Creek Park
Public Communications were closed at 7:15 p.m.
Council member Pacheco commented that there was no evidence that he had done anything wrong towards an Executive staff member and emphasized the importance of his Council colleagues to exercise discretion. He expressed his belief that the investigation was a waste of taxpayers' money
CONSENT CALENDAR
Motion: Approve CONSENT CALENDAR with the exception of Item #6
Moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Council member Marlen Garcia.
1. WARRANTS AND DEMANDS
Staff Report
City Council received and filed.
2. PROPOSED RECOGNITIONS BY THE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL FOR THE PERIOD OF OCTOBER 7, 2009 THROUGH OCTOBER 20, 2009
Staff Report
City Council approved the preparation and presentation of the plaques and certificates as outlined in the staff report.
3. MINUTES
Staff Report
City Council approved the minutes of the special and regular meetings of September 2, 2009.
4. CITY TREASURER’S REPORT - AUGUST 2009
Staff Report
City Council received and filed.
5. APPROVAL TO RELEASE FUNDS ALLOCATED BY THE OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY (OTS) FOR THE "SOBRIETY CHECKPOINT MINI-GRANT PROGRAM" AND "CLICK IT OR TICKET MINI-GRANT PROGRAM" GRANTS
Staff Report
City Council 1) authorized the release of funds allocated by the Office of Traffic Safety and 2) authorized the Chief of Police or her designee complete any required documents for processing the purchase of equipment and for acquiring the grant funds.
The following item was pulled by Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia for separate discussion:
6. AWARD A CONTRACT FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF THE MC NEILL MANOR TENANT IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
Staff Report
Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia spoke about how the city was using the stimulus funds to improve the community; proposed that when the city receives stimulus funds, staff look at the criteria, such as how many jobs will be created locally,how many families will be impacted and benefit from these projects. Requested that a local hiring ordinance be looked into that creates jobs and apprenticeship opportunities, as well as project labor agreements.
She requested that the matter be agendized for the next meeting, stating that the City should be maximizing its opportunities with the stimulus finds as they would not always be available.
Motion: 1) award a Construction Contract to Titanium Construction Group, Inc. in the amount of $137,230; 2) authorize the Chief Executive Officer to execute the Contract as soon as the HUD documents and other funding forms have been verified; and 3) authorize the Director of Public Works to execute any necessary change orders to reduce the contract cost or to revise work items so that construction costs do not exceed the available funding.
Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia, seconded by Mayor Lozano.
7. APPROVAL TO RELEASE FUNDS ALLOCATED BY THE OFFICE OF COMMUNITY ORIENTED POLICING (COPS) GRANT
Staff Report
City Council 1) authorized the release of funds allocated by the Office of Community Oriented Policing Services to purchase radio upgrades and 2) authorized the Chief of Police or her designee to complete any required documents for processing the purchase of equipment and for acquiring the grant funds.
SET MATTERS - PUBLIC HEARINGS
8. CITY COUNCIL CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF THE RELEASE OF FUNDS ALLOCATED BY THE RECOVERY ACT EDWARD BYRNE MEMORIAL JUSTICE ASSISTANCE GRANT (JAG) PROGRAM AND TO ENTER INTO A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES TO ADMINISTER THE GRANT
Staff Report
Chief Hadsell presented the report. Mayor Lozano opened the public hearing for those wishing to speak in favor or opposition. Seeing no interest the public hearing was closed
Motion: waive further reading, read by title only and adopt Resolution No. 2009-041 entitled, "A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF BALDWIN PARK EXPRESSING SUPPORT FOR AND APPROVING THE APPLICATION FOR THE RECOVERY ACT EDWARD BYRNE MEMORIAL JUSTICE ASSISTANCE GRANT (JAG) PROGRAM" and authorize the Chief Executive Officer to sign the Recovery Act Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Baldwin Park and the City of Los Angeles.
Moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia.
REPORTS OF OFFICERS
NONE
CITY COUNCIL/ CITY CLERK / CITY TREASURER / STAFF REQUESTS & COMMUNICATIONS
Request by Mayor Lozano, Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia & Council Members Marlen Garcia & Bejarano for discussion & follow-up to the approved June 3, 2009 motion to undertake an investigation of the alleged berating of an Executive staff member by Council member Pacheco
Council member Bejarano made the following statement:
At the Council meeting of June 3, 2009, and in order to best protect the City from possible liability, Mayor Lozano, Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia and Council members Marlen Garcia and myself passed a motion directing staff to undertake an investigation of the alleged berating of an Executive staff member by Council member Pacheco . That investigation is now complete. Due to the personnel-related nature of that report it must remain confidential. Neither the original investigation report nor any copy of that report is being retained at City Hall or by any member of the City Council or City staff.
Fortunately, the special investigator hired by the City found Council member Pacheco did not violate any State or Federal laws prohibiting harrassment during this incident. However, the investigator did find Council member Pacheco had inappropriately exceeded his authority as a Council member by berating the Executive staff member and not following City protocol, policies and regulations regarding interaction with staff and conveying concerns he may have with staff members' performance. The investigator also determined such actions could seriously undermine any staff members ability to carry out their duties and responsibilities. The investigator also determined that if Council member Pacheco were to continue with this type of behavior, it could potentially subject the City to liability.
Four-fifths of the City Council members find those types of actions to be outside of the course and scope of any Council members' duty and authority as a council member. Four-fifths of the City Council members also insist that Council member Pacheco not engage in any similar behavior in the future.
To again protect the City from potential liability, Council member Pacheco is hereby put on notice if he conducts himself in a inappropriate manner similar to that described in the investigation reort and that conduct results in an legal action being pursued, then the City (i) will not pay for the legal defense of that action on behalf of Council member Pacheco, (ii) will not pay any damages or costs that may be awarded against Council member Pacheco as a result of that litigation and (iii) will seek recovery of the fees and cost for any legal defense and any award of damages and costs that may be suffered by the City if the City is named in such a lawsuit.
Motion: To have the minutes of this meeting reflect the comments of Council member Bejarano verbatim
Moved by Council member Bejarano, seconded by Council member Marlen Garcia.
Council member Pacheco responded to the comments regarding the investigation and the actions of his Council colleagues and requested that the political attacks end
Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia requested from Chief Executive Officer Singhal and Public Works Director Galvez an update on the issue at Landis Avenue & School Street; she requested an update on the Green Vision program / advisory committee and an update from Chief Hadsell on any policy revisions to the noise ordinance
Council member Marlen Garcia announced the Community Design Fair and expressed the importance of the participation of Baldwin Park residents to become advocates for their community
Mayor Pro Tem Monica Garcia reiterated her request to agendize discussion of project labor agreements for the next meeting. Council member Pacheco expressed his strong support of project labor agreements and spoke about their importance
ADJOURNMENT
There being no other matters for discussion the meeting was adjourned at 7:31 p.m.
Approved as presented by the Council at their meeting held October 21, 2009.
Laura M. Nieto, CMC
Deputy City Clerk
